candidates.title: Design spec still shows the deleted fixed close-wave timeout as the canonical exec example
candidates.detail: The `exec` example for `takt close-wave` still reads `"timeout_s": 1800` — the exact value of the now-deleted `closeTimeoutS` constant. This diff removes that constant and makes the close-wave exec op's timeout_s a computed value (`sessionSeconds(deadline.Close(deadline.Budget{...}))`, spec A2.2), which generally will not be 1800 (it scales with VerifyCommands/ReviewTasks/BackendTimeout/VerifyTimeout and is strictly greater than deadline.Close's own result). This is the master design reference under docs/superpowers/specs/ that the rubric names explicitly, and it now documents the pre-A2.2 fixed-timeout behaviour this wave's diff replaces. The spec/plan docs that guided this task (docs/takt/lets-work-on-60-and-62/plan.md and spec.md) do not list this file among the ones to update, so nothing else in the run addresses it.

verdicts.evidence: internal/decide/decide.go's fixed `closeTimeoutS = 1800` constant is deleted by this diff and the close-wave `exec` op's timeout_s is replaced with `sessionSeconds(deadline.Close(deadline.Budget{VerifyTimeout: f.VerifyTimeout, VerifyCommands: f.Wave.VerifyCommands, BackendTimeout: f.BackendTimeout, ReviewTasks: f.Wave.ReviewTasks, MaxParallel: st.Config.MaxParallel}))` (wave-2.s1.a2.diff, decide.go hunk around line 307). The design spec's `exec` example still hard-codes the old value verbatim: `{ "op": "exec", "narration": "closing wave 0: verify + review 3 tasks", "command": "takt close-wave --slug cedar-policy-2154", "timeout_s": 1800 }` at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-24-takt-design.md:462, and a repo-wide grep confirms this is the only mention of `1800`/`timeout_s`/`deadline.Close`/`internal/deadline` in that file, so nothing nearby already reflects the new derivation. Checked for a later mitigation: task 8 (plan.index.json id 8, class docs, the only task after task 4 that touches this file) is scoped to exactly four edits — README.md:151-152, the design doc's §12 config example (lines 1133-1134, the `"timeout": "5m"` backend example, unrelated), the §13 'Timeouts everywhere' bullet (lines 1178-1179), and §7.5/§5.2 prose about pr-archive cleanup (lines 886, 480-481, for issue #62) — none of which is line 462 or the exec example's `timeout_s` value; task 8's verify greps (checked in plan.index.json) likewise never touch `timeout_s` or `1800`. The docs lens rubric for this wave explicitly names 'the design specs under docs/superpowers/specs/' as required reading, matching the candidate's claim that the rubric names this file. No existing mitigation found.
